Stated Claim / Post Context:
Democrat Peggy Flanagan Beats Republican Michele Tafoya for Minnesota Senate Seat

Democrat Peggy Flanagan, the lieutenant governor of Minnesota, has beaten Republican media personality Michele Tafoya for the state's open U.S. Senate seat.
The post Democrat Peggy Flanagan Beats Republican Michele Tafoya for Minnesota Senate Seat appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Democrat Peggy Flanagan, the lieutenant governor of Minnesota, has beaten Republican media personality Michele Tafoya for the state’s open U.S. Senate seat.

The race was called for Flanagan by NBC News a few hours after polls closed on Tuesday night. As of 10:45 p.m., the senator-elect had 54.5 percent of the vote over Tafoya’s 42.7 percent, with nearly 90 percent of the votes tallied.

Tafoya, a former sports broadcaster, entered the race in January and handily won the August Republican primary over former Navy SEAL Adam Schwarze and former basketball player Royce White.

In the Democratic primary, Flanagan joined in on the trend of progressive left-wing candidates beating more moderate liberals this midterm season in her solid defeat of Rep. Angie Craig (D-MN).

In a statement after the race was called, Flanagan said the results proved that “the many can beat the money, and that no president can ever beat the power of the people.”

The seat became open after Sen. Tina Smith (D-MN) announced in the beginning of 2025 that she would not seek another term. Smith threw her support behind Flanagan earlier this year, calling her a “fierce fighter” who has “delivered results for Minnesotans.”

Just last Monday, President Donald Trump claimed that the only way for Tafoya to lose was if Democrats cheated.

“Don’t allow them to play with the Votes after the race is over. The Federal Government will be watching closely,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “The only way she can lose is if they cheat by playing games with the Ballots as they come in.”

Olivia Rondeau is a politics reporter for Breitbart News based in Washington, DC. Find her on X/Twitter and Instagram.

[Source 2 — nypost.com (Bias: Right / Tabloid Conservative)] (URL: https://nypost.com/2026/11/04/us-news/henry-cuellar-texas-democrat-pardoned-by-trump-wins-12th-house-term/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Henry Cuellar, Texas Democrat pardoned by Trump, wins 12th House term

Cuellar, 71, and his wife Imelda had been indicted in May 2024 on bribery and money laundering charges, but were pardoned by Trump in December 2025.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Rep. Henry Cuellar, a Texas Democrat who received a pardon from President Trump after being indicted on corruption charges, easily won a 12th House term on Tuesday.

Cuellar led Republican nominee Tano Tijerina by 66% to 30% with about 80% of the ballots tallied.

Cuellar, 71, and his wife Imelda had been indicted in May 2024 on bribery and money laundering charges. With the case still pending, Trump pardoned the couple this past December, claiming Cuellar had been targeted by the Biden Justice Department for attacking the 46th president’s open borders policy.

Days later, after Cuellar confirmed he would run for another term, Trump turned on the congressman, bashing him for not switching parties and claiming he only pardoned the Cuellars after their daughters pleaded with him to do so.

“Such a lack of LOYALTY, something that Texas Voters, and Henry’s daughters, will not like,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social Dec. 7. “Oh’ well, next time, no more Mr. Nice guy!”

Republicans saw a chance to pick up Cuellar’s seat and recruited Tijerina, a local elected judge, to run against him.

Despite House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) and Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.) both campaigning alongside Tijerina, Cuellar lived up to his reputation as the “King of Laredo.”

Two weeks before the election, with polls showing Tijerina well behind, GOP-supporting outside groups stopped spending on the race, opting to move their money elsewhere.

Meanwhile, former President Bill Clinton endorsed Cuellar, along with Democratic Majority for Israel and the American Israel Political Affairs Committee.

Prosecutors claimed Henry and Imelda Cuellar accepted hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes from an Azerbaijani oil and gas company as well as a Mexican bank in exchange for the congressman working to sway US policy to benefit both the central Asian nation and the financial institution.
